text: Preliminary findings show that we may require some upgrades at various levels, including the consumer intake substations, the distribution grid network, as well as power generation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The required upgrades will be implemented over the next two decades as we survey our grid and gather insights on charging behaviour.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Agencies plan upgrades by catering for a capacity buffer to insure against unanticipated consumption growth.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is a major undertaking which will necessarily involve some electrical infrastructure upgrades, and LTA has launched a Request-for-Information to consult the industry on how best to structure private sector involvement in the funding of these upgrades.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Input from this exercise will also inform the design and use of carpark lots for charging, including issues that Mr Dennis Tan had mentioned.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Ms Janet Ang pointed out, agencies will need to work closely together on the national charger deployment plan.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We already see this close cooperation among agencies in the pilot charging point tender issued in November 2020, covering multiple carparks owned by different agencies.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Another example, as mentioned by Mr Sharael Taha, is how LTA is working with HDB to incorporate EV charging demand into the upgrading of substations in older estates, under HDB's Electrical Load Upgrading Programme.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Going forward, the National EV Centre under LTA will coordinate and drive close collaboration among agencies, including URA, EMA and HDB, to deploy chargers.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will also explore supporting regulations on data use, which Ms Mariam Jaafar has suggested.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I am glad that Mr Louis Ng and Ms Janet Ang raised the role of private development owners in the deployment of EV charging points.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To kick this off, we will launch the EV Common Charger Grant in July, to defray charger installation costs in non-landed private residences, such as condominiums.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We will need to engage stakeholders, such as MCSTs, managing agents and charging operators, to see if we can do more.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Users must find it more worthwhile to drive an EV compared to an internal combustion engine vehicle, so that vendors will enter the market.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Beyond charger deployment, the issue of charging anxiety raised by Ms Ng Ling Ling can be addressed by maximising access to chargers as far as possible through a mix of smart charging solutions and advance booking features.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: To respond to Mr Gan Thiam Poh, our charger deployment tenders will also incorporate innovations in charging technology where feasible.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: More importantly, as Ms Janet Ang rightly pointed out, developing good social norms is also essential to discourage behaviour like lot hogging by cars that do not need charging.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As Mr Dennis Tan mentioned, there are pricing schemes to discourage such behaviour, such as time-based pricing for an EV that is already fully charged.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We agree with Ms Yeo Wan Ling that point-to-point transport (P2P) drivers have specific charging needs which need to be met as they transit to EVs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are working closely with P2P transport operators to facilitate their efforts to develop charging infrastructure for their fleets.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: P2P drivers can also tap on the growing network of fast chargers island-wide.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Sixth, on the disposal and recycling of used EV batteries, an issue which Mr Leon Perera raised.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Some of these ideas are beyond the scope of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Today's Bill to assign LTA statutory functions on EV and EV infrastructure is a strong commitment to the transition to cleaner energy vehicles, but it is only the first step.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Building on this, we will introduce further legislation in due course, such as the registration of EV chargers and charger provision requirement for new buildings.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Nevertheless, we will study and, where possible, incorporate the many useful ideas and also address the concerns raised by Members today.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The Government will do this in partnership with industry and public stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In particular, echoing what Ms Janet Ang said, there is much economic value offered by the EV industry.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are working with relevant economic agencies to anchor high value R&D activities and develop related industries, such as charging systems and automotive manufacturing, to establish an EV eco-system.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As highlighted by Mr Sharael Taha, our workforce, especially our technicians and mechanics, will need to be equipped with the necessary skills to transit into future job opportunities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We are working closely with a wide variety of stakeholders on this: unions, trade associations, companies, Institutes of Higher Learning and skills development agencies.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Through our combined efforts, I look forward to making a safe transition to EVs and a greener, more sustainable living environment.
